entries.title: More than 1,300 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
entries.snippet: Hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations in France, with protests also taking place in other European countries.

entries.title: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates

entries.title: Voters in Brazil head to polls as Lula goes up against Bolsonaro's son
entries.snippet: Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of Brazil's imprisoned ex-president, is challenging Lula, who is seeking a fourth term in office.

entries.title: Musk says SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection as service restored
entries.snippet: The tech billionaire accuses Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using the network for military activity.

entries.title: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in north-east Nigeria
entries.snippet: Police are searching for other casualties, with officials warning the actual death toll could rise further.

entries.title: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
entries.snippet: Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany.

entries.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
entries.snippet: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.

entries.title: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
entries.snippet: Nayib Bukele says bodies delivered to soldiers are "not our men" amid search for Salvadorans abducted last week.

entries.title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
entries.snippet: Obama said the election was "the last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration".

entries.title: Mum who died trying to save sons was hero, husband says
entries.snippet: Nathan Gregory says the loss of childhood sweetheart Leanne "is unimaginable for our family".

entries.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
entries.snippet: She was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

entries.title: Australian MP's condition improves after alleged car attack
entries.snippet: The independent MP is now in a serious but stable condition, according to the Melbourne hospital.

entries.title: From Russian cages to Irish sanctuary: The five-year rescue journey of Bu and Tyapa
entries.snippet: For Bu and Tyapa, the five-year journey from Russia to the Irish countryside was anything but straightforward.

entries.title: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
entries.snippet: Three people - two women and one man - have been released, and one person remains in custody, gardaí say.

entries.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save

entries.title: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
entries.snippet: The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests to form the biggest challenge to Vučić's rule.

entries.title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
entries.snippet: From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on some products, including certain machinery, and placed on others, such as carpets.

entries.title: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
entries.snippet: Police have launched a manhunt for the building's owner and contractor after the multi-storey building collapsed while still under construction.

entries.title: Trump administration sues to block certification of upcoming Alaska election
entries.snippet: The justice department has filed a lawsuit arguing that the inclusion of two candidates named Dan Sullivan could confuse voters.

entries.title: Minneapolis withdrawal was 'surrender', Trump's ex-border patrol chief tells BBC
entries.snippet: Greg Bovino was the public face of the controversial immigration enforcement operation in the city earlier this year.

entries.title: The College of Magic turns ordinary kids into confident, top-hat wearing magicians
entries.snippet: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.

entries.title: When a teen posts a selfie, how much filter is 'too much' filter?
entries.snippet: The recent Meta settlement includes a clause banning "cosmetic procedure filters" for teens. But defining what constitutes an extreme makeover isn't easy.

entries.title: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are
entries.snippet: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.

entries.title: Independent candidates sense a moment in the West. Democrats are hoping they're right
entries.snippet: As they look to win the Senate, Democrats are hoping that independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana can help them topple Republicans in a part of the country where their own brand is hurting.

entries.title: In Arkansas, Democrats see an opening at the edge of the competitive midterms map
entries.snippet: In a sign of the potentially dire midterm political environment, Republicans have spent millions of dollars playing defense in Arkansas, one of the most conservative states in the country.

entries.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe
entries.snippet: While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.

entries.title: Drought, fire and high diesel prices 'addin' up tough' for Oregon ranchers
entries.snippet: Record diesel prices are kicking Western ranchers while they're down. Drought means they have to buy extra hay, and pay truckers extra to deliver it because of fuel price hikes.

entries.title: Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement over sexual abuse claims
entries.snippet: The 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy members and lay workers have all agreed to the settlement, according to an attorney for some of the plaintiffs.

entries.title: Trade tariffs cause whiplash at Port Milwaukee
entries.snippet: Sacha Pfeiffer visits Port Milwaukee to see how President Trump's tariffs have affected the flow of goods and impacted the regional economy.

entries.title: How data centers became a bipartisan political issue in Wisconsin
entries.snippet: Data centers are a big issue across the country. As midterms approach, many look to the swing state of Wisconsin for lessons for how that issue could play out nationally.

entries.title: Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida
entries.snippet: Trump has been criticized in the past for voting by mail despite his long history of railing against that method of submitting ballots.

entries.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe
entries.snippet: The demonstration in Milan remained peaceful, but there were brief clashes with police in both Rome and Turin.

entries.title: New York state woman charged with voting illegally says she recently learned she wasn't a citizen
entries.snippet: Marva Cook was adopted as a toddler and had always assumed she was a U.S. citizen, she told Homeland Security investigators earlier this month, according to the criminal complaint.

entries.title: Six Flags says it will install seat belts on Georgia roller coaster after rider's death
entries.snippet: The theme park operator announced the extra safeguard less than two weeks after 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem of Atlanta died after being ejected from his seat on the Goliath coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia.

entries.title: More than 400,000 protest across France, challenging Macron as Paris clashes erupt
entries.snippet: Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to a close Saturday, with more than 400,000 people rallying across France over school funding and soaring living costs in a fresh challenge to President Emmanuel Macron. Police made nearly 1,000 arrests, the government said.

entries.title: What's going on with Dan Sullivan and Dan Sullivan? The Alaska Senate litigation, explained
entries.snippet: One of them is a Republican senator and ally of the president. The other is a retired schoolteacher whom Republicans accuse of being a Democratic plant to siphon away votes.

entries.title: Musk says he was behind Starlink speed restriction after service in Ukraine is restored
entries.snippet: Questions have persisted since last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Kyiv has relied on for years to counter Moscow's attacks.

entries.title: U.S. is reducing staffing at 4 Middle East embassies over increased threats from Iran
entries.snippet: In a memo sent Friday to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said his teams "have received intelligence that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel."

entries.title: DOJ orders some California counties to set aside ballots from suspected noncitizens
entries.snippet: The letters are the latest escalation in a legal battle between California and President Donald Trump's Department of Justice, which has recently focused on the state in its efforts to root out noncitizen voting ahead of the midterm elections.

entries.title: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visits China to inaugurate a new cross-border bridge
entries.snippet: Kim's visit to China is his latest move in an increasingly assertive foreign policy as he seeks to align Pyongyang with Beijing and Moscow in a united front against the United States under what he portrays as a "new Cold War." It's his first visit in a year.

entries.title: Rollins says USDA is 'full-bore ahead' on Forest Service reorganization
entries.snippet: The Trump administration wants to move Forest Service headquarters from Washington to Salt Lake City, shutter 23 research stations, and close many regional offices and replace them with state offices.

entries.title: Signs of fraying loyalty emerge in Netanyahu stronghold before Israeli election
entries.snippet: Kiryat Shmona, Israel's northernmost city, has long been a bastion of support for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party. But that loyalty is no longer ironclad.

entries.title: Treasury proposes rule to curb high-tech investments in China and other adversaries
entries.snippet: The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other "countries of concern."

entries.title: Trump says he ordered suit to block Alaska Senate results if GOP loses

entries.title: Seeking to help Collins in Maine, Trump exempts some Canadian imports from his 50% tariffs

entries.title: Surging diesel prices loom over Republicans in Iowa's midterm races

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Brazil votes in tight runoff between leftist Lula and right-wing Flavio Bolsonaro
entries.snippet: The high stakes election will decide whether Brazil will move toward the right or retain a leftist government.

entries.title: India news: Rahul Gandhi urges protest against voter deletions, announces November 1 rally
entries.snippet: India's opposition leader Rahul Gandhi has accused the ruling BJP of "vote theft" and urged people to join a rally in Delhi on November 1. The call comes amid protests over revision of electoral rolls. DW has more.

entries.title: Serbia votes in closely fought election as student-led opposition challenges Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power
entries.snippet: Nearly two years after a deadly railway station collapse sparked mass anti-corruption protests, Serbians are voting in a closely fought election that could end Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power.

entries.title: Germany news: Fire flares up at Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat
entries.snippet: Fire broke out again overnight at a former mountain retreat used by Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler. Meanwhile, a survey shows most people in Germany feel the days of the governing coalition are numbered. DW has more.

entries.title: Gadi Eisenkot campaigns on Moroccan roots in challenge to Netanyahu
entries.snippet: As Israel prepares to vote, Gadi Eisenkot is leveraging his Moroccan heritage in Likud strongholds such as Sderot. From historical divides to October 7, identity and trauma are redefining the city's political loyalties.

entries.title: Prague honours Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
entries.snippet: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia looks to US for an AI edge as Yemen's Houthis up pressure
entries.snippet: The US is helping Saudi Arabia fight the Houthi group in Yemen with AI-assisted targeting. But AI is not a magic bullet, experts say, and there are technological, political and human rights issues to consider.

entries.title: Bulgaria holds presidential elections amid divisions over Ukraine war
entries.snippet: Bulgarians are voting in presidential elections amid security concerns over attacks on ships in the Black Sea. The vote for the largely ceremonial post is seen as a test of the popularity of Prime Minister Rumen Radev.

entries.title: Trump announces Audi will build $4 billion factory in US
entries.snippet: After Donald Trump made the announcement at an election rally in Georgia, the German carmaker confirmed plans for a factory in the US state, but noted car production would only start early next decade.

entries.title: New York Archdiocese to pay $800 million to sex abuse survivors
entries.snippet: Around 1,300 survivors agreed to the $800 million payout from the Catholic Church, marking one of the largest clergy abuse settlements in the US.

entries.title: Nigeria: Tinubu launches reelection bid amid economic woes
entries.snippet: President Bola Tinubu promised "a better tomorrow" for Nigerians while kicking off his next electoral campaign, while also blaming his rivals for poverty plaguing Africa's most populous nation.

entries.title: Ukraine: Starlink satellite speeds restored to normal
entries.snippet: The announcement comes after Starlink and Starshield restrictions had disrupted military operations in Ukraine and sparked tensions with the US.

entries.title: German national facing trial for alleged attempt to join IS
entries.snippet: A 21-year-old suspect is being held in pre-trial detention for allegedly trying to join the "Islamic State" terror group.

entries.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
entries.snippet: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

entries.title: Will Guinea-Bissau remain trapped in political chaos?
entries.snippet: Elections scheduled for December 6 in Guinea-Bissau have been postponed indefinitely. No new date has been set, leaving the country's return to civilian rule uncertain.

entries.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
entries.snippet: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

entries.title: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un travels to Chinese border city via newly opened bridge
entries.snippet: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un travelled to China’s border city of Dandong via a newly opened bridge linking the two countries, where he met a senior Chinese official.

entries.title: Why Russia's arrest of Japanese journalist is the latest sign of deteriorating ties between the countries.
entries.snippet: Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. The Kremlin claims that Japan is using journalists as spies.

entries.title: Taiwan: Typhoon Champi leaves 1 dead, over 500 injured
entries.snippet: After killing one person and causing major disruptions in Taiwan, Typhoon Champi is now headed towards China.
